page.layout: One page of text: running head at top centre; a four-line verse epigram above a rule; then a heading and a poem of verse lines in the main column; a catchword "IN" at the lower right.

main_text.p:
Vt recto auertit sanas à tramite mentes,
Ex improbis sic reddit homines pessimos.
Assentatores fugiat quicumque Veretur
Vltrò perenne accersere sibi dedecus.
At quanto satius monitorem audire seuerum,
Laudare parcum, liberalem carpere!
main_text.head: IN EBRIOSOS.

p.i:
VOs farciendo deditos abdomini,
Mortem haurientes Unde Vitam cateri,
Quos mane primum, feráque Videt Vespera
Mensa assidentes, poculisque grandibus,
Infame donec sitis intuentibus,
Foedam Vomentes crapulam, spectaculum:
Homines quis esse credat istis Vultibus?
Liuentibus tot fronte picta pustulis?
Naso pyropis tot madente marcidis?
Cingente limbo oculos rubentes coccino?
Oculis fluore turgidis Vinaceo?
Ritu madente? diffluentibus genis?
Vos immò quisnam comparauit bestiis?
Namque ebriosas nemo Vidit bestias.
Qua sorte dignos ergo Vos censebimus?
Hac scilicet. Vinos Vt ebrietas suos
Afficere poenis quibus amatores solet,
Vos Vsque & Vsque strenuè distorqueat,
Tumuloque stratos perpetua premat sitis.

page.notes: The epigram above the rule and the verse below are set in roman and italic type; long s rendered as s. Some words in the first lines of the poem are damaged by ink and uncertain: "Unde"/"Vitam" and several "V" forms in the italic lines may be printed "V" for "U" in the original and are transcribed as shown. The initial "V" of "Vos" is a large woodcut-style initial. Faint marks on the right margin are not text.
